::: {#exm-datasheet}

#### A datasheet for the digits

Part of a [datasheet](#def-datasheet) for the digits of this page,
from the description that comes with them [@alpaydin1998optdigits]:

- **Why:** the description does not say;
  the first use it lists is a 1995 thesis on combining classifiers to recognize handwritten digits.
- **What:** 5,620 images of digits in all,
  each an 8 by 8 grid of counts from 0 to 16,
  with its digit as the label.
  43 people wrote them:
  30 wrote the 3,823 training images,
  and 13 others wrote the 1,797 test images used on this page.
  No other facts about the writers are recorded.
- **Collection:** the digits were written on a preprinted form,
  and programs from the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology turned them into 32 by 32 bitmaps.
- **Cleaning:** each 32 by 32 image was cut into 4 by 4 blocks,
  and the number of on pixels in each block counted.
- **Uses:** the authors kept the test writers apart from the training writers,
  to measure [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) on new writers.
- **Distribution:** the UCI Machine Learning Repository, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
  under a CC BY 4.0 license.

The description does not say who maintains the data.
A [model card](#def-model-card) for a network trained on these digits can point to this datasheet for its training and evaluation data.

:::
